idni-80-update.label: Follow-up comment on IDNI/tau-testnet #80 (validator request)
idni-80-update.text: Quick update from our side. The node behind this request has been running since Oct 27 at node.tauhud.com and is fully synced to the tip (status: https://tauhud.com/status/). The key stays idle until it appears in the active set; the node will not propose before that (validator-gate patch, infra/node/patches in jimb000o/tau-command-hud). Pubkey again for convenience: 80ad4a20099a0d9002c67ffd0094587c2238fbe84d24d41861481936bce25779a64f4ba12ef7825051a9507f11d536b8. Happy to adjust anything on our end, or to test a second validator on a staging genesis first if that is easier for you. Thanks!

launch-hn-comment.label: Hacker News: your first comment under the Show HN post (open your post, paste, press add comment)
launch-hn-comment.text:
Hi HN. Tau HUD is an unofficial, community-built live view of Tau Testnet Alpha, the public test network of Tau, run by IDNI.

What makes Tau unusual: the chain's own rules (fees, who seals blocks, how many votes a change needs) are written in a logic language. A proposed rule is checked before it can apply, and it becomes law once enough participants vote for it, with no hard fork and no admin key. Each account can also set rules of its own for its money, which the node enforces.

The site runs its own node and relay and shows blocks, proposals and votes as they happen. The real testnet is quiet (one validator, few transactions), so every page also has a clearly marked Simulation mode: a deterministic made-up chain generated in your browser, where you can watch or practise a rule change by vote from start to finish.

Things to try: the Explorer ("what happened to my transaction?"), Time travel (the rules in force at any block), the Rule Playground, and Vote, a step-by-step guide to casting a real vote with IDNI's own command line.

Static site, MIT licensed, no cookies or tracking: https://github.com/jimb000o/tau-command-hud. Testnet tokens have no value and nothing is sold. Feedback is very welcome, especially on what is confusing.

launch-tg-tau.label: Tau community on Telegram: introduce Tau HUD
launch-tg-tau.text:
Hi everyone. I have been building Tau HUD, an unofficial community dashboard for Tau Testnet Alpha: https://tauhud.com

It runs its own node and shows blocks, proposals and votes as they happen. Also there:
· Explorer: what happened to a transaction, block or address
· Time travel: the rules in force at any block
· Rule Playground: write a rule and run the testnet's own checks on it
· Vote: a step-by-step guide to vote on the real testnet with the tau-testnet CLI, practised first in a simulation
· The Daily Consensus, a weekly 1920s style newspaper of the testnet

Alerts for every rule change and chain restart: t.me/tauHUDcom and x.com/TauHUDcom

Not affiliated with IDNI, testnet AGRS have no value. Feedback and bug reports are very welcome.

launch-tg-own.text:
Tau HUD goes public today

Until now this channel and the site grew quietly. Today we are telling the Tau community, Hacker News and Reddit about it.

Every page now has a Share card (in the About menu and in every footer) with its own preview picture. If one page helped you understand Tau, send it to one person who would like it.
